request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 0 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means results are clear-cut and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means the top configs are too close to call or something looks off. You can inspect the per-fold PR-AUC breakdown of any completed run to assess consistency. A config that wins consistently across folds is more trustworthy than one with high variance. (Independent run 1, no feature agent.)

concerns: Run 1 (LightGBM, all features, no imbalance handling) leads run 3 by 0.0204 PR-AUC, which is under one SD (about 0.068). By the simplicity rule this is not a significant gain. Run 3 is the same model family with a smaller, more regularised setup, and it is not simpler in any meaningful way.
Run 1 does beat run 2, the random forest, by 0.0475, which is still under one SD. The random forest is not clearly simpler than LightGBM, so run 1 stays the pick on the point estimate.

Run 1 beats runs 2 and 3 in every fold, so the ranking is consistent. Fold 3 is weak for all three runs (0.57 to 0.63), which suggests that fold is harder or has a different composition. The fold SD of about 0.07 is large relative to the gaps between configs.

Run 1 uses the 'all' feature set, which includes size or volume features. These can proxy for provider scale rather than suspicious behaviour. The no_size run 3 is only about 0.02 lower, so most of the signal does not depend on size. Run 1's small edge may partly reflect size leakage.

ROC-AUC of about 0.943 and PR-AUC of about 0.73 at 9.35% prevalence are strong for this task. The PotentialFraud label has undocumented origin and may be rule-derived or correlated with the features, so this performance may reflect label-generation artefacts and not real fraud detection. Treat the results with suspicion.

Precision@50 is 0.764 for run 1 and 0.772 for run 3, so the top of the queue is essentially tied. The audit queue is about 100 providers, and precision@100 was not reported. With only 5 folds and 3 configs tried, the search is very narrow.
Fold splits are not described. If the same provider's claims or related providers span folds, or if there is no time-based split over the 2008-2009 window, the estimates could be optimistic.
